question: How do I stop needing other people's approval?
seo_title: How to Stop Needing Approval: A Biblical Answer | TheWrkShop
description: Wanting approval is human. Needing it to feel okay is bondage. How to tell the difference and find your identity in Christ, from Galatians 1:10.
answer: You don't stop needing approval by caring less about people; you stop by letting God's approval settle your identity first. Wanting to be valued is normal. Needing approval to feel okay means people's opinions have become your master. In Christ you are already approved, so applause can't add to you and rejection can't take anything away.

sections.heading: Wanting approval vs. needing it
paragraphs: "I appreciate being valued" is gratitude. "I need approval to feel okay" is bondage. The difference shows up in decisions: the extra work you take on because you fear disappointing your boss, the honest conversation you avoid, the convictions you soften when certain people are in the room.

sections.heading: Fear of man is giving people authority over your identity
paragraphs: It happens when their approval decides your peace, their criticism decides your confidence, and their acceptance decides your decisions. At that point they aren't influencing you. They're ruling you.

Jesus loved people deeply and still disappointed them constantly. He could, because before He performed a single miracle the Father had already said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased." Identity came before performance. Most men reverse that order.

sections.heading: Freedom makes you better at loving people, not worse
paragraphs: When you no longer need someone's approval, you're finally free to serve them honestly. You can tell the truth instead of what they want to hear. The goal isn't to become cold or unteachable. It's to live for an audience of One.

scriptures.text: Am I now trying to win the approval of human beings, or of God? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
Fear of man will prove to be a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe.
For they loved human praise more than praise from God.

steps: Look back over last week. Name one decision you made mainly to avoid disappointing someone.
Ask: "If I weren't worried about their reaction, would I decide the same way?"
Tomorrow, before you check your phone, ask God one question: "What would please You today?"

faqs.q: Is it wrong to want people to like me?
faqs.a: No. Healthy relationships include appreciation and respect. It becomes a problem when approval becomes necessary for your identity, or when it can override what God has said.

faqs.q: What does the Bible call people-pleasing?
faqs.a: Scripture calls it the fear of man (Proverbs 29:25). Galatians 1:10 says that if pleasing people is your primary goal, serving Christ can't be.

faqs.q: How do I stop people-pleasing without becoming harsh?
faqs.a: Replace it, don't just remove it. The opposite of people-pleasing isn't indifference; it's honest love. Ask what Christ would look like in the conversation, then do that kindly.
